stem.text: Let \( f(x) = \begin{cases} \frac{x^{2} - 16}{x + 4}, & x < -4 \\ kx + m, & -4 \le x \le -3 \\ 2 x^{2} - 8, & x > -3 \end{cases} \), where k and m are constants. Find the values of k and m for which f is continuous for all real numbers. Show that the function value at each boundary agrees with both one sided limits.

answer_key.label: \( k = 18 \) and \( m = 64 \), because the middle branch must equal -8 at \( x = -4 \) and 10 at \( x = -3 \).

worked_solution.text: For \( x < -4 \), \( \frac{x^{2} - 16}{x + 4} = x - 4 \), so the limit from the left at \( x = -4 \) is -8. The middle branch gives \( f(-4) = -4k + m \), so \( -4k + m = -8 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: match the branches at the first boundary

worked_solution.text: At \( x = -3 \) the middle branch gives \( f(-3) = -3k + m \) and the last branch approaches 10, so \( -3k + m = 10 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: match the branches at the second boundary

worked_solution.text: Subtracting the equations gives \( k = 18 \), and then \( m = 64 \).

options.label: \( k = 18 \) and \( m = 64 \), because the middle branch must equal -8 at \( x = -4 \) and 10 at \( x = -3 \).
\( k = 1 \) and \( m = -4 \), because the middle branch must equal -8 at \( x = -4 \) and -7 at \( x = -3 \).
options.derivation: at x = -3 the first branch, which applies only for x < -4, used in place of the last branch

options.label: \( k = -14 \) and \( m = -32 \), because the middle branch must equal 24 at \( x = -4 \) and 10 at \( x = -3 \).
options.derivation: at x = -4 the last branch, which applies only for x > -3, used in place of the first branch

options.label: No values of k and m work, because \( \frac{x^{2} - 16}{x + 4} \) is undefined at \( x = -4 \), so f has no limit there.
options.derivation: the first branch is undefined at x = -4, and that was taken to mean its limit there does not exist
